title: whisper.cpp failed to read audio file with .m4a on Mac (convert to WAV with afconvert)
short_title: whisper.cpp won't read your .m4a? Convert it to WAV

runs.cmd: cd "$(mktemp -d)" && say -o interview.m4a --data-format=aac "Thanks for talking with me today." && /opt/homebrew/bin/whisper-cli -m ~/whisper-models/ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin -f interview.m4a -np
runs.output:
read_audio_data: failed to read audio data
error: failed to read audio file 'interview.m4a'

runs.cmd: cd "$(mktemp -d)" && say -o interview.m4a --data-format=aac "Thanks for talking with me today." && afconvert -f WAVE -d LEI16@16000 -c 1 interview.m4a interview.wav && afinfo interview.wav | grep "Data format" && /opt/homebrew/bin/whisper-cli -m ~/whisper-models/ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin -f interview.wav -np -nt
runs.output:
Data format:     1 ch,  16000 Hz, Int16
Thanks for talking with me today.

verify.notes: Built 2026-11-22 on Ben's Mac in mktemp folders with whisper.cpp 1.9.5 from Homebrew and the ggml-large-v3-turbo model. The test recording is one sentence made with the built-in say command as AAC in an .m4a file, the format Voice Memos and most iPhone recordings use. Run 1 shows whisper-cli failing to decode it with its built-in miniaudio decoder. Run 2 converts it with afconvert, which ships with macOS, to 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV, confirms the format with afinfo, and transcribes it. The whisper.cpp README says whisper-cli runs only with 16-bit WAV files and to convert input first. GitHub issue 4011 is a Homebrew whisper-cli user on macOS 26 hitting the same four lines with an AAC .m4a podcast while MP3 worked. Tapefolio claims are from its page: it transcribes audio and video files on your Mac, such as .m4a, .mp3, .mp4 and .mov, with word timing, and nothing you open is uploaded.
